narrative:
Inventory optimization analysis for material PL1__MF765B09 reveals a SMOOTH demand pattern with mean daily demand of 520.2 units and CV of 0.33. 
A significant declining trend was detected (slope=-0.72 units/day, p=0.0001). 
Lead time exhibits VOLATILE behavior (CV=0.66) with mean 1.43 days. 
The dominant variance component is lead time variability (85.1%), indicating that supply chain reliability improvements would have the greatest impact on buffer requirements.

The recommended policy establishes a safety stock of 869 units and order quantity of 7091 units, providing 95% service level protection. 
This results in a reorder point of 1612 units with an order frequency of approximately every 13.6 days.

Compared to the SAP baseline policy (safety stock=0, order quantity=838), the recommended approach reduces total annual costs by $5,855.97 (73.8% savings) 
through optimized order batching while maintaining superior service levels through appropriate buffer sizing.

Storage capacity constraint of 9254 units is satisfied with peak inventory of 7960 units.
